# 16. QA

<!-- Generated by tools/build_checklists.py. Edit the generator to change checklist structure. -->

**Purpose:** Verify the final static site behaves correctly across content, devices, browsers, accessibility modes, search requirements, and launch conditions.

## Universal Constraints
- [ ] The solution must remain static front-end only: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, images, fonts, documents, and generated static files only.
- [ ] The stack must avoid proprietary lock-in, paid builders, paid plugins, closed hosting features that cannot be replaced, and opaque third-party scripts where an open or free-tier-friendly alternative exists.
- [ ] Every decision must be documented as a quality rule, acceptance criterion, or exception with rationale; implementation notes belong outside the checklist.
- [ ] Every checklist item must be testable by review, automated audit, source inspection, browser testing, or client sign-off.
- [ ] Manual exceptions must record the owner, reason, expiration date, affected pages, and residual risk.

## Must Exist
- [ ] A QA matrix covering pages, templates, browsers, devices, breakpoints, zoom levels, forms, languages, and launch-critical journeys.
- [ ] A defect severity model for blockers, major defects, minor defects, content defects, and enhancements.
- [ ] A regression checklist for navigation, forms, metadata, assets, accessibility, performance, analytics, and hosting.
- [ ] A browser support list covering current Chromium, Firefox, Safari, mobile Safari, and Android Chrome where audience requires it.
- [ ] A device test plan including small mobile, large mobile, tablet, laptop, desktop, high-density display, and reduced-motion settings.
- [ ] A content QA checklist for spelling, grammar, names, dates, legal notices, pricing, phone numbers, addresses, and claims.
- [ ] A production smoke test checklist run after deployment.
- [ ] A sign-off record for client, content, design, development, SEO, accessibility, and legal stakeholders where applicable.

## Must Be True
- [ ] QA must test the deployed static output, not only source files or local previews.
- [ ] Every critical journey must pass on mobile and desktop.
- [ ] Every form, external link, phone link, email link, download, and CTA must be tested.
- [ ] Visual QA must use real production content and realistic content extremes.
- [ ] Accessibility QA must include manual keyboard testing.
- [ ] SEO QA must use production URLs and final domain metadata.
- [ ] Analytics QA must verify event firing, consent behavior, and exclusion of personal data.
- [ ] No blocker or major defect may remain at launch without explicit written acceptance.

## Must Be Checked
- [ ] Check all internal links, anchors, downloads, canonical URLs, hreflang URLs, and sitemap URLs.
- [ ] Check that layout does not break at 320px width, common mobile widths, 1024px, 1440px, wide desktop, and zoom.
- [ ] Check that images load, lazy load appropriately, have dimensions, and preserve aspect ratio.
- [ ] Check that JavaScript errors do not appear during normal navigation and form use.
- [ ] Check that 404, offline-like failure, slow network, and blocked third-party scripts produce acceptable behavior.
- [ ] Check that cache, redirects, headers, and HTTPS work after deployment.
- [ ] Check that no draft content, TODOs, test data, lorem ipsum, or staging URLs remain.
- [ ] Check that generated reports are stored with launch artifacts.

## Must Be Avoided
- [ ] Avoid QA based only on desktop Chrome.
- [ ] Avoid launching immediately after a large unreviewed content or dependency change.
- [ ] Avoid accepting visual defects caused by translated or long real content.
- [ ] Avoid relying only on automated scores.
- [ ] Avoid testing forms only with happy-path input.
- [ ] Avoid ignoring console errors because the page appears to render.

## Premium Acceptance Standard
- [ ] QA must create confidence that the site works for real users in real deployment conditions.
- [ ] Every defect must have owner, severity, page, reproduction notes, and resolution state.
- [ ] Launch must be a controlled decision, not the first full test.
- [ ] Post-launch QA must confirm that production behavior matches signed-off behavior.

## Automation Hooks
- [ ] Use the audit script for repeatable static checks and JSON reports.
- [ ] Use optional free browser automation with Playwright for screenshot, navigation, and form smoke tests.

## Detailed Best-Practice Review Areas
- [ ] Global QA covers site completion, static-site integrity, standalone pages, no placeholders, no broken layouts, correct folders, and static host suitability.
- [ ] Page-by-page QA covers planned pages, correct URLs, hero, logical sections, final CTA, header/footer, spacing, headings, uniqueness, conversion path, and desktop/mobile completeness.
- [ ] Header, footer, navigation, layout, responsive breakpoints, orientation, typography, visual design, image, video/media, buttons/links, forms, JavaScript, animation, accessibility, SEO, performance, browser, content, contact/conversion, analytics/tracking, cookie/privacy, security/safety, deployment, 404/edge cases, blog, portfolio/case study, static e-commerce, industry-specific, final manual QA, and launch approval are all checked.
- [ ] Manual QA clicks every header link, footer link, CTA, form, menu, dropdown, accordion, tab, slider, filter, anchor, external link, social link, and floating widget.
- [ ] Launch approval requires all pages, links, buttons, forms, menus, dropdowns, CTAs, images, videos/fallbacks, scripts, metadata, favicon, sitemap, robots, 404, legal pages, and analytics where required.

## Report Output Required
- [ ] Report every failed automated check with severity, checklist category, issue code, affected file or page, evidence, whether it is script-fixable, and how to fix it.
- [ ] Report every manual-only failure with reviewer, affected page or component, expected standard, actual behavior, recommended fix, owner, and target date.
- [ ] Separate launch blockers from quality improvements so critical static-site failures cannot be hidden by low-priority polish notes.
- [ ] Attach the JSON audit report, Markdown audit report, screenshots where visual proof is needed, and manual QA evidence for browser, device, keyboard, screen reader, form, analytics, and live deployment checks.

## Evidence Required
- [ ] Record reviewed pages, tools used, dates, reviewers, unresolved exceptions, and links to generated reports.
- [ ] Attach screenshots or source references for failures that cannot be proven by automated reports.
- [ ] Mark checklist items as complete only when the production static output satisfies the rule.
